record.original_question: Can one detect from the joint spectrum of a quantum integrabl e system T1,hbar,..., Tn,hbar that a singularity is degenerate? The theory of semitoric systems provides a strong motivation for u nderstanding the connections be- tween integrable systems and Hamiltonian torus actions. In view of t his, we conclude by discussing a possible quantum approach to counting fixed points of symplectic S1-actions. In view of Tolman's recent work constructing a non-Hamiltonian symp lectic S1-action on a compact manifold with isolated fixed points, the questions how many fixed point s symplectic actions have (both upper and lower bounds) and what the relation between having fixed points and being Hamiltonian 38 is, have attracted much interest [214, 92, 184, 93]. See also Pelayo [180] for a discussion and other references. As far as we know, the "quantised" version of this pr oblem is not well understood, although some steps have been taken in this direction [148]. The object to qua ntise can no longer be the momentum map, since there is no momentum map - however, McDuff po inted out in [164] that any symplectic S1-action admits an S1-valued momentum map mu: M → S1. The explicit construction of this map appears in [182], and it can be quantised [148, Section 7] (her e the operator will be unitary, rather than self-adjoint).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a compact connected symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$, and let $F=(f_1,\dots,f_n):M\to\mathbb{R}^n$ be a completely integrable system, i.e. smooth functions whose Poisson brackets satisfy $\{f_i,f_j\}=0$ and whose differentials are almost everywhere linearly independent. A point $p\in M$ is a singularity of $F$ if $\mathrm{rank}\,dF(p)<n$; such a singularity is called non-degenerate if, in suitable symplectic coordinates, the Hessians of $f_1,\dots,f_n$ span a Cartan subalgebra of $\mathfrak{sp}(2n,\mathbb{R})$, and is called degenerate otherwise.

A semiclassical quantization of $F$ is a family of commuting self-adjoint operators $T_{1,\hbar},\dots,T_{n,\hbar}$ (depending on $\hbar\in(0,\hbar_0]$) acting on Hilbert spaces $\mathcal{H}_\hbar$, whose principal symbols are $f_1,\dots,f_n$ and which satisfy the standard axioms of semiclassical pseudodifferential or Berezin–Toeplitz quantization. The joint spectrum $\mathrm{JointSpec}(T_{1,\hbar},\dots,T_{n,\hbar})$ is the set of tuples $(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n$ such that there exists a nonzero common eigenvector $v\in\mathcal{H}_\hbar$ with $T_{j,\hbar}v=\lambda_j v$ for all $j$.

Problem: Given the joint spectrum $\mathrm{JointSpec}(T_{1,\hbar},\dots,T_{n,\hbar})$ as $\hbar\to 0$, devise a procedure (or prove the existence of one) that determines whether the underlying classical integrable system $F$ has a degenerate singularity. Equivalently, can the property "$F$ has a degenerate critical point" be read off from the asymptotic structure of the joint spectrum?
artifact.category_tag: Inverse spectral theory of integrable systems
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Le Floch–Pelayo and collaborators) on inverse spectral theory for semitoric and Jaynes–Cummings-type quantum integrable systems has produced algorithmic procedures to recover symplectic invariants near non-degenerate (focus-focus) singularities from the joint spectrum, but no general result detecting degeneracy of singularities from the joint spectrum for arbitrary quantum integrable systems has been established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The inverse spectral problem for quantum semitoric systems
status_evidence.snippet: first algorithmic inverse spectral result that holds for a large class of quantum integrable systems ... semitoric systems are completely spectrally determined
status_evidence.claim: Progress focuses on non-degenerate (semitoric) systems; the question of detecting degeneracy in general remains open.

status_evidence.title: Isospectrality for quantum toric integrable systems
status_evidence.snippet: Joint spectrum determines classical toric system
status_evidence.claim: Inverse spectral results exist for toric/semitoric cases but not addressing general degenerate singularities.
